title: Shared contracts, data and evidence
summary: Own cross-component records, data and evaluation controls, composition semantics and reproducibility; operation and encoder Heroes own their specific behavior.

goals.title: Establish shared research contracts
goals.description: Keep the common record vocabulary and evidence standards usable across components.

milestones.title: Adopt the operation charter and stable capability IDs
milestones.description: The project scope and repository guidance use ORR-DESIGN-001 v0.1.0 and its OR-01 through OR-13 families.
acceptance: README and project instructions identify the charter, stable capability families and required contract/evidence records.

milestones.title: Implement common record and compatibility validation
milestones.description: Define reusable ObservationRef, SpaceRef, EmbeddingRecord, OperationRun and EvidenceRecord validation from the charter. Distinguish record identity, space/configuration identity, fitted-artifact identity and runtime response identity; validate operation-specific input roles rather than comparing dimensions or requiring universal space equality.
acceptance: The shared contract preserves observed embeddings, task-specific latent states, predicted states, transformed candidates and generated content as distinguishable kinds with source/parent lineage; derived records cannot manufacture observation provenance.

A SpaceRef resolves the selected instance/revision policy, checkpoint or provider identity, preprocessing and fitted transforms, native output selector/layout, dimensions and normalization. Per-request IDs and response hashes belong to execution/record provenance, not a new coordinate space per sample.

A compatibility check declares its operation and operand roles and returns an explicit supported relationship or a typed rejection. Equal dimensions or a shared family/model alias do not suffice; distinct query/document roles or an admitted directional OR-10 mapping can be valid relationships.

Unknown/incompatible relationships, malformed or non-finite records, stale fitted artifacts and temporal violations do not produce ordinary successful outputs. Define success, abstention and failure separately, with reason codes; fallback or partial-output policies must be explicit and preserve denominator/coverage accounting.

Conformance fixtures include same-shape/different-instance vectors, changed preprocessing, stale indexes, allowed query/document roles, an admitted mapping with retained provenance, and rejected role/kind conversions. This is engineering evidence only.

milestones.title: Separate work readiness, run admission and claim support
milestones.description: Define a lightweight staged workflow without changing the current dashboard status enum. Preserve Contract → Implementation → Evaluation ownership while allowing reusable interface authoring and bounded development before confirmatory admission.
acceptance: Keep existing Hero IDs, schemaVersion and status values until the repository consumer schema is inspected and any schema migration is explicitly adopted. Express current prerequisites and blockers in descriptions/acceptance; do not label unbound work contract-ready or mark new work complete from this review.

Separate reusable-interface authoring, binding an experimental instance, admitting an execution, and accepting a scientific claim. The Operation Contract and linked Requirements-and-Evidence Record are required for each experimental run, but compact records may reuse shared rules rather than copy the whole charter.

Every experimental execution identifies its purpose (diagnostic/development, confirmatory operation, or pipeline evaluation), permitted claim, exact inputs/artifacts/configuration, resources and permissions, and evidence destination. Unresolved bindings block only the dependent execution, not drafting or unrelated engineering work.

Readiness blockers identify the missing dependency and the condition that clears it; authorization pauses cannot be cleared by scheduling, diagnostic labels or another Hero. A future dependency/readiness field requires validated consumer-schema support rather than ad hoc new status values.

Track execution disposition separately from claim verdict. Completed valid negative or inconclusive evaluations can finish their scoped work; failed, aborted or invalid attempts stay visible without being treated as supporting operation evidence.

evidence.label: Proposed corrections and acceptance rationale; not execution evidence

goals.title: Establish shared data and comparison controls
goals.description: Register source identities and keep fitted preprocessing, splits and comparisons reproducible.

milestones.title: Select a dataset manifest and comparison protocol
milestones.description: Choose an explicitly admitted initial dataset and population; record access/license, source versions/hashes, splits, dependency intervals, fitted preprocessing and matched-input/capacity controls. The dashboard itself selects no dataset, checkpoint or experiment; authoring the reusable data contract does not require these choices to be invented.
acceptance: The bound dataset manifest identifies actual permitted source snapshots or synthetic generator/configuration, units/entities, time semantics, labels and their availability, source hashes, split membership and known overlap or duplicate relations.

Fit every learned artifact only on its permitted fit population, including encoder adaptation, scaling/imputation, learned pooling or dimensionality reduction, mapping anchors, indexes/reference models, thresholds, readouts and model-selection decisions. Record pretrained exposure as known, unknown or excluded by design rather than assuming a frozen encoder has no assessment exposure.

Time-series splits and exclusions derive from actual feature/target dependency intervals and shared sources, not timestamps alone or an unexplained fixed gap. Distinguish development, calibration and protected assessment; declared online reference updates are part of the evaluated policy.

Baselines specify matched accessible information and an explicit capacity/compute/cost budget or explain unavoidable differences. Entity/trajectory dependence determines the sampling and uncertainty unit; dense overlapping windows are not silently treated as independent replicates.

Maintain a selection/exposure history for diagnostics, parameter search and repeated assessments. Revised protocols use fresh confirmation data or explicitly report exploratory scope; historical evidence is not overwritten or rescored by a new dashboard.

milestones.title: Enforce temporal integrity across every derived path
milestones.description: Define shared information-availability semantics for all temporally indexed inputs and descendants, including RPB, MTF and CPB outputs. Distinguish an observation’s event time, source/dependency support and availability from a run’s declared as-of boundary and the availability/exposure of fitted artifacts.
acceptance: Each applicable record resolves an event/support interval, a dependency/availability bound, source revision or vintage, and any per-position validity mask with explicit time meaning. A mask alone or a window-end label is not a substitute for knowing which inputs influenced an output. Non-temporal uses declare and justify non-applicability.

Each run declares retrospective, point-in-time/as-of, or another explicit temporal claim. For an as-of claim, all observed/feature dependencies and permitted fit/model-selection information must satisfy its cutoff; future target values may enter scoring only through the evaluator after predictions are fixed. Unknown training/provider exposure narrows the claim and does not become a fabricated timestamp.

Derived records carry the maximum required input-availability boundary and full lineage, or a documented tighter per-output dependency proof. Aggregation, alignment, retrieval and rollout cannot erase unavailable dependencies; predicted-state target time remains distinct from its information origin.

Test suffix perturbations at the boundary claimed by the output: an end-of-window representation may use its complete available window, whereas prefix outputs need prefix-valid dependence. CPB naming or a padded-input mask is not, by itself, an empirical temporal-integrity receipt.

Negative fixtures cover future-window contamination, fitted-preprocessing leakage, delayed/revised labels, future reference/index entries, and an unavailable input carried through a transform/composition. Test point-in-time model availability separately from retrospective frozen-encoder recoverability; report the evidence scope.

A reconstructed walk-forward simulation may compute artifacts today from permitted earlier inputs; distinguish it from actual historical deployment and record its allowed fit/selection information. File creation time alone neither proves nor disproves point-in-time eligibility.

The contract specifies typed rejection or explicit downgrade to a different admitted retrospective mode when cutoff evidence is missing. A downstream consumer may not silently weaken the temporal claim.

evidence.label: Proposed corrections and acceptance rationale; not execution evidence

milestones.title: Retain and index every run disposition and claim verdict
milestones.description: Define one discoverable, versioned evidence namespace covering positive, negative, inconclusive, invalid, failed, aborted and admission-rejected work. Keep historical model-owned records in place and link them rather than rewriting their protocols.
acceptance: Adopt or explicitly replace the proposed namespace research/orr/: contracts/, requirements/, runs/<run-id>/, evidence/ and index.jsonl. These are proposed repository locations, not claims that a registry exists. The index identifies owner Hero, purpose, contract/RER revisions, dataset/SpaceRefs, protocol, disposition, claim verdict and artifact locations.

Register an attempt before experimental execution and finalize it even on error or interruption; record rejected admissions as such without inventing an executed run. Distinguish completed/non-supporting evidence from invalid methodology and execution failure.

Retain manifests, relevant permitted artifacts or immutable artifact references/digests, logs, exclusions, seeds/configuration, environment/code identity, metrics and uncertainty. Explicitly record unavailable or policy-restricted artifacts and the resulting replay limitation; never store credentials or unauthorized raw content.

Finalized evidence records are append-only or versioned with explicit supersession/correction links. Index checks detect dangling references, digest mismatches, stale status, and lost failed/inconclusive records; restricted-content deletion leaves an auditable permitted tombstone.

A charter link is a normative/design reference, not a test receipt. Completing new milestones requires their actual accepted artifacts and checks; preserved historical done milestones remain scoped assertions until their referenced receipts are independently inspected.

evidence.label: Proposed corrections and acceptance rationale; not execution evidence

goals.title: Preserve reproducibility and pipeline meaning
goals.description: Maintain the verified environment and require end-to-end evidence for composed claims.

milestones.title: Verify the managed environment and preserved import
milestones.description: The migration retained the original files and research records, reused the managed Linux environment and passed the scoped engineering verification.
acceptance: Migration verification records zero file mismatches, unchanged model C++/headers and no SDK mutations.
The environment receipt records the pinned managed container and offline dependency verification.

milestones.title: Migrate active maintenance tools from Python
milestones.description: The owner-requested first migration tranche switches SDK verification, layout checks, compiled source fingerprints and dashboard artwork preparation to the existing Node/C++ stack. Retained research protocols and frozen Python evidence remain separate; encoder research stays paused.
acceptance: Active maintenance entry points use the shared pinned Linux Node runtime and a container-built C++ artwork helper; setup remains dependency-only and introduces no downloads or npm packages.
Independent fixtures pass with Python commands blocked, and migration comparisons preserve SDK proof/inventory values, source fingerprints, archive integrity, artwork bytes and provenance.
Archived and hash-bound original sources remain available; the migration record explicitly identifies the research scripts that still require a separate migration.

milestones.title: Define pipeline edge semantics and end-to-end evaluation
milestones.description: For every admitted composition, declare each edge’s record kind, role/SpaceRef relationship, availability propagation, fitted-artifact dependencies and failure policy. Component conformance, component utility and end-to-end utility remain separate evidence claims.
acceptance: Each edge identifies producer/consumer contract versions, payload schema/kind, source and derived SpaceRefs, operation-specific compatibility check or mapping, dependency/availability propagation, and failure/abstention/partial-output behavior.

Each fitted component and index/reference artifact is bound to its fit data, configuration and validity scope. Altering a provider, preprocessing, mapping, fit population or schema triggers an explicit affected-artifact review/rebuild; old evidence and artifacts remain identifiable rather than silently blessed for the new path.

No predicted or generated record becomes an observation by crossing an edge; no unavailable input loses its temporal restriction; and no failed record becomes an ordinary zero vector, success, missing row or action. Any predeclared fallback has its own path identity and evaluation coverage.

The end-to-end protocol records the full admitted population and denominator, baselines, costs, exclusions and failure/abstention rates. Component evidence is linked but cannot stand in for an executed pipeline evaluation.

Exercise at least one deliberate mismatch, temporal violation and upstream failure through a complete small path; assert propagated result states and evidence indexing before making any composed quality claim.

milestones.title: Close one bounded provider-to-operation evidence loop
milestones.description: Use a proposed selected-RPB-instance → OR-01 exact-retrieval path as the first bounded integration candidate. This priority is not selection of a checkpoint, dataset or experimental admission; other families remain independent proposed work and CPB stays paused.
acceptance: Bind an available RPB version, trained checkpoint, preprocessing/output contract, permitted fixed synthetic or public dataset, corpus/query split, independent relevance rule, metric, k, tie handling, baselines, uncertainty unit and budget. Missing instance/data evidence is a named blocker, not a guessed default.

Freeze the Operation Contract and linked Requirements-and-Evidence Record with the two-stage scope: engineering conformance first, then only the declared bounded retrieval question. No future-risk, latent-dynamics, causal, cross-modal or real-world generalization claim is implied.

Exercise one temporal-compatible end-of-window provider path and exact retrieval with a frozen eligible corpus; define source-overlap/self/duplicate exclusions. Use a simple matched-input raw-descriptor baseline and a declared chance/random-ranking reference where appropriate.

Run deliberate incompatible-space, unavailable/future candidate, non-finite-input and propagated-failure fixtures. Index engineering outcomes separately from any held-out relevance result and replay the pipeline from its retained permitted artifacts.

Close the loop with a valid scoped conclusion, including a negative or inconclusive result. Synthetic fixture success alone establishes only the specified synthetic/engineering scope; no model is declared a winner or universally adopted by this milestone.

evidence.label: Proposed corrections and acceptance rationale; not execution evidence

goals.title: Complete the language migration with bounded scientific Python
goals.description: Completed the requested engineering language migration in the existing managed container. Maintained preparation and metadata use Node/Bash; independent scientific Python remains deliberate. All eighty baseline sources and original callers are accounted for. Acceptance covers artificial mechanics, current caller/source wiring and compilation, with frozen evidence and research pauses preserved.

milestones.title: Account for every source, caller and retained scientific responsibility
milestones.description: Validated the complete eighty-file, fifty-nine-caller inventory, all 161 original command sites and thirty-four embedded blocks against current source. Original hashes, retained scientific responsibilities, historical module pins and reader failure/repair identities remain explicit. New implementations and encodings have separate identities.
acceptance: Reconcile every baseline source, caller, shebang and embedded block to a maintained Node replacement, a retired refusal or an explicitly justified scientific Python responsibility, preserving original reference hashes.

Validate the complete disposition and current caller/source closure against the source inventory; distinguish historical references and narrow mixed scientific APIs from maintained Python metadata commands.

Preserve old reader failure/repair provenance and historical pins. New implementation/serialization/path adapters receive separate identities; unavailable saved witnesses are not regenerated by retraining or fitting.

evidence.label: Complete language disposition and original identities
Tested source identities and observed results

milestones.title: Move all maintained preparation and record keeping to Node
milestones.description: Ten input-preparation helpers have fixture-tested policies, exact role matrices, argument handling and actual Make source-list coverage. Node owns all thirty-four embedded metadata blocks and four SDK proof snippets. Separate positive CLI fixtures cover eight protocol preparations, two captures and five summaries. No package or image change was required.
acceptance: Validate all ten preparation helpers through policy, role, parser and actual Make source-list fixtures; confirm Node CLI caller wiring and exercise protocol metadata CLIs with artificial inputs through the pinned runtime.

Preserve the 195 TRAIN-file/15-instance and 85 TRAIN/VALIDATION role contracts. Admit complete path/alias/size matrices before payload hashes, detect source/input changes and retain exclusive durable publication.
Bind every transitive runtime/source dependency to the compiled or captured closure. Keep generic mechanisms versioned under shared/artifacts and owning policies in embeddings.
Identify new JSON encoding, exact integer/mean behavior and any strengthened admission rule explicitly; do not replace historical hashed byte identities with new serializer output.

evidence.label: Shared artifact contract and artificial fixtures
Tested source identities and observed results

milestones.title: Preserve independent scientific checks and isolate native candidates
milestones.description: Seven retained scientific suites passed 105 tests in ordinary and optimized Python modes, plus both strict reader SOURCE fixture programs. Frozen codec pins still resolve to their unchanged archived bytes. Native reader/math engineering candidates passed their isolated tests and remain unadopted; each future changed-reader run still requires its own admitted source seal.
acceptance: Record and verify every retained scientific Python role and dependency, including capacity tensor bind and the structured reader's captured Python contract API. Their metadata CLIs use Node.
Preserve exact arithmetic, seeds, masks, support/abstention, ties, tolerances, gate verdicts and failure outcomes; only explicit physical path/admission changes are introduced by integration.

Keep frozen codec hashes unchanged and resolve them through declared archived paths. Retain failed-reader evidence and require a separately identified source-fixture seal for changed reader implementations.

Keep optional native reader/math candidates isolated. Their engineering checks do not replace or certify the scientific Python reference; any adoption requires separately admitted closed-format and numerical parity evidence.

evidence.label: Scientific responsibilities and explicit physical mapping
Implementation limits and native candidate boundary
Tested source identities and observed results

milestones.title: Complete protocol metadata adapters and preserve numerical auditors
milestones.description: Protocol metadata paths and retired refusals are wired to Node. Artificial family and CLI fixtures passed for preparation, capture, summaries, capsule dispatch/lifecycle mechanics and gate outcomes. Numerical publishers and tensor-association audits remain Python. These fixtures do not claim full historical executions or saved-quality equivalence.
acceptance: Validate Node preparation, source capture, capsule lifecycle mechanics and metadata summaries through artificial family/CLI fixtures, preserving cohort/repetition/role rules and negative or unsupported outcomes. Full historical executions remain separately bound research.

Require completed hash-bound independent saved checks before metadata summaries; retain numerical publication audits even when their command is named publish. No automatic promotion, fitting, training or new held-out access is introduced.
Preserve selected-field and complete-role admission before scientific payload access, including the full eighteen-role capacity observation/witness matrix and the TRAIN-only diagnostic boundary.

Keep all six historical registry/global-summary publishers retired with Python-free refusals. New receipt encodings and rendered reports identify their implementation and uncertified equivalence scope.

evidence.label: Complete protocol implementation and retained auditor rationale
Tested source identities and observed results

milestones.title: Wire the entire maintained caller and build surface
milestones.description: All 24 actual Make source closures passed after deletion, with no missing source, retired Python helper or omitted production Node import. Thirty affected C++ translation units compiled with authoritative flags and actual source/Git identities. Current physical paths, original historical identities and nine unchanged inherited generic objects are explicitly bound. Only declared scientific Python remains in maintained source.
acceptance: Verify current direct, absolute, versioned, shebang and transitive interpreter use against the closed retained-scientific policy; no Python metadata command or implicit fallback remains.

Validate Make/source closure and CLI argument compatibility through fixture-only paths and inert producers. Build/cache/tmp products stay under named /opt/mityane-geometrics directories and new selected outputs under .temp.
Verify explicit original-to-current path mappings in both Node and C++ without rewriting historical receipts. Retained artifacts and the original SDK remain in place.
Normal maintenance and dashboard tools retain their tested Python-free paths. Root setup remains dependency-only and no image/package change or experiment execution is part of the migration.

evidence.label: Tested source identities and observed results

milestones.title: Validate the complete language boundary in the managed container
milestones.description: All 40 obsolete Python working copies are deleted; only the 40 declared scientific Python files remain in maintained source. Post-removal checks passed: 109 Node fixtures, 210 scientific test executions, strict reader SOURCE fixtures, 24 actual Make closures, 69 maintenance tests, offline setup, artwork and 30 C++ translation units. All 6,424 frozen archive files and nine inherited shared objects remain unchanged. Dashboard refresh and freshness complete closure. Historical scientific equivalence and paused research remain separately admitted.
acceptance: Run the complete source/Node/path-mapping/scientific artificial fixture suite through the existing managed container, resolve failures and record the exact tested source identities and environment.

Accept the engineered metadata/path boundary without requiring a real historical saved-quality rerun. Retained scientific references, new receipt encodings, native scientific-reader adoption and future per-run seals keep separate identities and admission requirements; do not infer historical numerical or serialized-byte equivalence.

Confirm all current callers obey the declared language boundary and every retained original has a preservation purpose. Retained scientific Python is an explicit accepted responsibility, not an unfinished metadata port.

Validate ordinary maintenance/setup entry points and refresh/check the dashboard after successful verification. Do not remove image packages, alter frozen archives or claim runtime equivalence from source inspection.

Remove every replaced Python working copy, verify its exact archived source identity and replacement, reject retired paths in current build closures, and require the maintained Python inventory to equal only the 40 declared scientific files.

evidence.label: Tested source identities and observed results

goals.title: Expose Hx14 capabilities as a reusable toolset
goals.description: Make the Hero's agreed shared contracts, compatibility checks, artifact/provenance and evidence helpers, and composition building blocks usable through common schemas, command-line tools and reusable APIs. Preserve component ownership and operation-specific semantics. This proposed goal does not resume deferred Hx14 work.

milestones.title: Define the shared tool surfaces and usage contracts
milestones.description: Map existing helpers and selected future building blocks to the common toolset, with explicit gaps and ownership; existing maintenance commands do not establish complete toolset coverage.
acceptance: Inventory the agreed contract, compatibility, artifact/provenance, evidence and composition surfaces, distinguishing implemented interfaces from proposed work and identifying their owning components.

Specify versioned CLI/API inputs, outputs, requirements, validation, success/abstention/failure behavior and retained provenance compatible with the common usage conventions; preserve operation-specific record kinds, roles, spaces and geometry.
Define bounded examples and completion criteria for the agreed surface without inventing a mandatory registry, resuming deferred work or treating engineering checks as scientific utility evidence.

milestones.title: Expose and verify the agreed shared building blocks
milestones.description: Deliver the agreed callable helpers, examples and integration checks in their owning components, retaining explicit compatibility and evidence boundaries.
acceptance: Expose the agreed shared building blocks through documented Linux CLI and reusable library interfaces, using the managed container and common versioned schemas without duplicating operation or provider behavior.

Verify the agreed standalone helpers and selected composed workflow, including incompatible records, artifact/provenance failures and propagated failures or abstentions; preserve denominators and saved-result inspection where applicable.

Retain actual engineering receipts and usage examples with explicit coverage and gaps. Keep credentials and restricted artifacts private; any scientific execution still requires its actual bindings, protocol and permissions.
